description:
A .NET wrapper library for FFmpeg using FFmpeg.AutoGen. This library provides a managed interface for FFmpeg's raw C API by wrapping around the unsafe pointers and structs provided by FFmpeg.AutoGen. It offers a higher-level, object-oriented approach to access and manipulate FFmpeg's core functionality, making it easier to integrate FFmpeg into .NET applications.

			Simplifies working with FFmpeg by providing a safer, managed wrapper around the native FFmpeg API.

			Exposes FFmpeg's powerful multimedia processing capabilities in a more accessible, object-oriented format.

			Reduces the need to work directly with pointers and memory management, leveraging the safety of C# for easier debugging and development.

			Ideal for .NET developers who need to integrate FFmpeg's audio and video processing, transcoding, streaming, and encoding/decoding capabilities in their applications.
releaseNotes:
FFmpeg 9.0.1 - "Lei"
			Version numbering scheme changed: FFMpegMajor.Major.Minor.Patch

			--- 9.9.1.0 ---
			Transcoder rewritten (breaking change), modelled on MediaSource/MediaSink and the ffmpeg command line tool:
			CopyStream, TranscodeStream (encoder, optional simple filter graph as with -vf/-af, configure callback, encoder options) and FilterStream (re-encode with the input codec) map the streams; Run, RunAsync, ProcessNext and Finish drive it.
			Filters can be given as a description string, as a factory (Func<FilterGraphContext, string> or FilterGraphFactory) that is called for every build with the input stream and the current frame format, or as an unconfigured FilterGraph object, which is copied (FilterGraph.Copy) for every build and therefore not recommended when the graph may have to be rebuilt.
			Each re-encoded audio/video stream runs through its own filter graph; encoder properties that are not set are taken from the filtered frames, the ones that are set (size, frame rate, pixel/sample format, sample rate, channel layout) are enforced. Graphs are rebuilt when the decoded format changes mid-stream.
			Start/Duration work like ffmpeg -ss (input) and -t: re-encoded streams are trimmed frame-exactly, copied streams start at the keyframe before Start. Audio decoders get enough preroll after seeking that initial padding no longer cuts into the range.
			Subtitles can be copied or re-encoded (with the decoder's subtitle header); chapters inside the range, metadata and dispositions are copied.
			ProgressChanged/Position/ExpectedDuration report progress; TryGetPreviewFrame/PreviewFrameUpdated give thread-safe preview frames (the PreviewFrame property was removed). Cancelling Run/RunAsync still finishes a valid output file.
			Fixed: scalers/resamplers were recreated for every frame and leaked, packets were mapped 1:1 to frames, encoders were opened before their extradata could reach the muxer header.
			Added: CodecContext.SubtitleHeader, AudioBufferSink.SetFrameSize, OptionQueryableBase.IsSetToDefault/TryIsSetToDefault.
			PlaybackEngine: SetVideoFilterFactory/SetAudioFilterFactory take the same factories as the Transcoder; they are called again whenever the graph is set up again (after seeking), instead of copying the graph.
			BugFix: FilterGraph.Copy (and therefore FilterGraph.Flush and the PlaybackEngine filters) failed for filters with unset options whose text form cannot be parsed back, e.g. aresample ("0 channels").
			BugFix: PlaybackEngine threw a NullReferenceException after a filter was removed (SetVideoFilter/SetAudioFilter with null).
			BugFix: CodecContext.ChannelLayout was read-only, so the channel layout of an encoder could not be set.
			BugFix: MediaSource.CodecContexts threw for inputs with streams without a decoder (data, attachments).

			--- 9.9.0.2 ---
			Many BugFixes found in a code review (also released for FFmpeg 8 as 8.1.2.14):
			IO: custom IOContext callbacks are rooted and no longer let exceptions escape into native code; IOContext/CodecContext can be finalized; use-after-free when opening custom IO failed; IOStreamContext no longer throws on construction; seeking works for seekable IOContexts.
			Formats/Codecs: MuxerContext double dispose, NoFile check and time base rescaling; FormatContext.Seekable returns None without an I/O context again; extradata is padded as FFmpeg requires; SendFrame no longer changes an open encoder's time base; encoded subtitle packets use a correct time base; MediaSource keeps its decoders, drains all of them at end of file and SeekExactly ends only for the requested stream; seeks past ~35 minutes and timestamp setters past ~6.6 hours no longer overflow.
			Utils: Rational +, - and int * Rational overflow; TimeSpan / Rational saturated; AVPacket leak and Size overrun; AVFrame.GetData/Copy/Size/Clone for bottom-up and audio frames; AVBuffer.ReplaceWith use-after-free; Move/Clone/Reference onto itself emptied the packet; AVResult64.ToString named wrong errors.
			Audio: AudioFifo layout conversion and peeks beyond one chunk, pinning of channel spans; SwrContext wrote past the buffer when converting at an offset; AudioBuffer Copy/MakeWriteable shared data through stale plane pointers, planar-to-packed copies were wrong; AudioClock counted time twice after Pause; ChannelLayout.Init kept a freed map after a failure.
			Collections: CircularArray.IndexOf/Clear, AVChapter removal keeps its order, SubtitleRect text setters crashed, hardware device/frames context references crashed when empty.
			Options: binary options were read from the wrong address; bool in SetOption(name, object); dictionary overloads use av_opt_set_dict2 and remove the entries that were set.
			MediaPlayer: VideoBuffer/AudioBuffer lost writes and CanSeek was reversed, AudioBuffer binary search could loop forever, SetBufferSize estimate, Stop state.
			Misc: SVTAV1.CreateAvif encoded the wrong frame; Transcoder decoded a packet twice; Logger kept no prefix state across av_log calls; FormatContext.Url is read as UTF-8; SwsContext throws if it cannot be created.
			Behaviour changes:
			TryGetOption(Option, out object): Color options are returned as string ("0xRRGGBBAA"), Duration as long (microseconds), array options as the string FFmpeg produces.
			SetOption(name, IDictionary) applies every entry as its own option (av_opt_set_dict2); `name` is not used.
			AudioBuffer.CopyTo/CopyToPacked throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException for a start index outside the buffer. SetBufferSize throws for a non-positive size or when no data rate can be determined.
			ChannelLayout custom channel names must be shorter than 16 bytes (UTF-8).
			PlaybackEngine: a decoding error now moves the player to Faulted and raises Faulted, it was only logged before.

			--- 9.9.0.1 ---
			BugFix: - Fixed a bug concerning the incorrect size of CLong/CULong on Windows or 32bit and netstandard.
			See AutoGen (v9.0.1.1) release notes for more details.
